 Tonight, voters are picking a new majority for Huntington Beach’s City Council, with the option to re-elect a slate of Republican councilmen or choose one of several new candidates for the four available seats on the city council. 
 Making noise where it matters. 
 You've read articles. Keep cranking up the volume on what's happening behind the scenes in Orange County with the Morning Report newsletter. Join 23,000 OC residents who rely on it.
 Did you catch that? 
 From local politics to the people and policies shaping our daily lives—it’s all in The Morning Report newsletter. Join 23,000 OC residents who rely on it.
 As of 10:30 p.m., Erin Spivey, Ben Davis, Taryn Palumbo, and incumbent Mayor Casey McKeon were on track to get a seat on the city council with over 22,000 votes apiece, with Councilman Pat Burns trailing behind Palumbo by 474 votes. 
 Mayor Casey McKeon, Councilmen Pat Burns, Andrew Gruel and Brian Thienes were all endorsed by the county Republican Party, while Erin Spivey, Taryn Palumbo, Ben Davis and Brenda Glim were all endorsed by the county Democratic Party. 
 The election comes four years after a Republican majority swept the 2024 election and initiated a number of controversial legal challenges against the state, arguing for city control over items like elections, housing and zoning.
